He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]]. He was highly regarded by scouts due to his {{height|ft=7|in=1}} wingspan and shooting ability. He attended [[Cardigan Mountain School]] in [[Canaan, New Hampshire]], and [[Westtown School]] in [[Westtown Township, Pennsylvania|West Chester, Pennsylvania]], and was considered one of the top high school prospects for the class of 2017. ==Early life== Bamba was born on May 12, 1998, in [[Harlem]], [[New York (state)|New York]] to Lancine Bamba and Aminata Johnson, who both emigrated from the [[Ivory Coast]].{{cite web|title=Mohamed Bamba|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/b/bamba-mohamed-2.aspx|website=[[USA Basketball]]|access-date=April 12, 2017|date=April 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170328200518/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/b/bamba-mohamed-2.aspx|archive-date=March 28, 2017|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|last1=Geoghegan|first1=Neil|title=Westtown star Mohamed Bamba tries to stay cool as spotlight grows brighter|url=http://papreplive.com/2017/02/20/westtown-star-mohamed-bamba-tries-to-stay-cool-as-spotlight-grows-brighter/|website=PA Prep Live|access-date=April 12, 2017|date=February 20, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170410052830/http://papreplive.com/2017/02/20/westtown-star-mohamed-bamba-tries-to-stay-cool-as-spotlight-grows-brighter/|archive-date=April 10, 2017|url-status=live}}{{cite web|last1=Slater|first1=Andrew|title=Blue Chip: 6'11" 2017 Five-Star Mohamed Bamba|url=https://247sports.com/college/duke/article/blue-chip-611-2017-five-star-mohamed-bamba-46129399/|website=[[247Sports.com]]|access-date=April 12, 2017|date=July 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160709230208/http://duke.247sports.com/Article/Blue-Chip-611-2017-Five-Star-Mohamed-Bamba-46129399|archive-date=July 9, 2016|url-status=live}} Bamba's grandparents were born and brought up in present-day [[Mali]]. Bamba made his official college debut on November 10, 2017, against [[2017–18 Northwestern State Demons basketball team|Northwestern State]], recording 15 points and eight rebounds in a blowout win that night. Eight days later, he recorded 13 points, 10 rebounds, and five blocks in a blowout win against [[2017–18 Lipscomb Bisons men's basketball team|Lipscomb]]. On December 30, Bamba recorded a season-high 22 points, 15 rebounds, and eight blocks in a loss to [[2017–18 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]]. On New Year's Day 2018, Bamba would record a then-season-high 16 rebounds with 10 points in a 74–70 overtime win over [[2017–18 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|Iowa State]]. He would record a new career-high in points scored with 25 points scored with 15 rebounds in an 85–72 win over [[2017–18 Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball team|Ole Miss]] on January 27, 2018, five days after recording his previous high of 24 points in a win over Iowa State. On February 17, Bamba would record a new career-high of 18 rebounds with 10 points scored in a 77–66 win over #23 ranked [[2017–18 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Oklahoma]], five days after tying his previous career-high of 16 rebounds with 16 points in a close 74–73 double overtime loss to [[2017–18 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]]. At the end of the regular season for Texas, Bamba was named a member of the Big 12's All-Newcomer Team and All-Defensive Team, as well as being named a member of the All-Big 12 Second Team. He averaged 12.9 points, 10.5 rebounds, and 0.5 assists per game. Following Texas's loss in the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA men's basketball tournament]] to [[2017–18 Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball team|Nevada]], Bamba announced his intention to forgo his final three seasons of collegiate eligibility and declare for the [[2018 NBA draft]], where he was expected to be a [[NBA draft lottery|lottery]] selection.{{Cite During the altercation, Bamba left the Magic bench area and threw punches at Timberwolves guard [[Austin Rivers]].{{Cite web |title=NBA Communications on Twitter: "The following was released by the NBA." |url=https://twitter.com/NBAPR/status/1622063768959127552 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=Twitter}} === Los Angeles Lakers (2023) === On February 9, 2023, Bamba was traded to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in a four-team trade involving the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-acquire-mo-bamba-and-davon-reed-2-9-23|title=Lakers Acquire Mo Bamba and Davon Reed|work=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023}}{{Cite web |title=Magic Acquire Patrick Beverley, Future Second Round Draft Pick and Cash Considerations as Part of a Four-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-acquire-patrick-beverley-future-second-round-draft-pick-cash-considerations-four-team-trade-la-lakers-mo-bamba-release-20230209 |date=February 9, 2023 |website=NBA.com|quote=the L.A. Lakers acquire Bamba from Orlando, Davon Reed from Denver, as well as two future second round draft picks (2024 and 2025 selections) from the L.A. Clippers}} On March 5, during a 113–105 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]], he played two minutes before suffering a left ankle injury and leaving the game.{{Cite web |title=Davis leads Lakers past Warriors 113-105 in Curry's return |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401469119 |access-date=March 9, 2023 |website=ESPN}} Four days later, the Lakers announced that Bamba had been diagnosed with a high left ankle sprain and would be sidelined for at least four weeks.{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers on Twitter: "Mo Bamba has been evaluated by Lakers team doctors and has been diagnosed with a high left ankle sprain. He will be re-evaluated in approximately four weeks." |url=https://twitter.com/Lakers/status/1633922030075801600 |access-date=March 9, 2023 |website=Twitter}} He returned to action on 7 April, playing as a substitute in a game against the [[Phoenix Suns]]. On June 29, 2023, Bamba was waived by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web |title=Lakers Waive Mo Bamba and Shaquille Harrison |url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/lakers-waive-mo-bamba-and-shaquille-harrison-6-29-23 |access-date=June 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2023–2024)=== On July 9, 2023, Bamba signed a one-year deal with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|title=Mo Bamba Signs with Sixers|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/mo-bamba-signs-with-76ers|website=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2023|access-date=July 9, 2023}} The Sixers' franchise player [[Joel Embiid]] insisted to Bamba that he join his team.{{cite web|title=Patrick Beverley says James Harden was a factor in picking the Sixers, and he wants him to stay |url=https://www.inquirer.com/sixers/sixers-patrick-beverley-mo-bamba-nba-free-agency-20230710.html|website=inquirer.com|date=July 12, 2023|author=Keith Pompey}} ===Los Angeles Clippers (2024–2025)=== On July 6, 2024, Bamba signed a one-year deal with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|author=LAClippers|title=LA Clippers Sign Mo Bamba|url=https://www.nba.com/clippers/news/la-clippers-sign-mo-bamba|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 7, 2024}} On February 1, 2025, Bamba, with [[P. On January 6, 2026, Bamba was waived by the Raptors.{{Cite web |title=Raptors waive depth centre Bamba after two-game stint |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nba/article/raptors-waive-depth-centre-bamba-after-two-game-stint/ |access-date=2026-01-11 |website=TSN.ca|language=en}} === Utah Jazz (2026–present) === On March 8, 2026, Bamba signed a 10–day contract with the [[Utah Jazz]].{{Cite web |title=Utah Jazz Sign Mo Bamba to Second 10-Day Contract {{!}} Utah Jazz |url=https://utahjazz.com/news/utah-jazz-sign-mo-bamba-to-second-10-day-contract |access-date=2026-03-15 |website=utahjazz.com |language=en}} In two appearances for the Jazz, he recorded averages of 5.0 points, 10.0 rebounds, and 0.5 assists. Out with an illness before a three-game road trip, Bamba's contract was terminated by the team on March 12.{{Cite web |date=2026-03-13 |title=Mo Bamba: Waived Thursday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/mo-bamba-waived-thursday/ |access-date=2026-03-15 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}} On July 8, 2026, Bamba re–signed with the Jazz on a two-year contract.{{Cite web |last=Koch |first=Jared |date=July 8, 2026 |title=Utah Jazz Sign Mo Bamba to 2-Year Contract: What It Means |url=https://www.si.com/nba/jazz/onsi/utah-jazz-sign-mo-bamba-to-2-year-contract-what-it-means |access-date=July 13, 2026 |website=Sports Illustrated}} ==National team career== Because of his Ivorian heritage, Bamba was eligible to play for the [[Ivory Coast men's national basketball team|Ivory Coast national team]].
